item.title: [SwiftHFR] App icon: set a badge iOS did not show again when the app is back on screen (#1060)
item.body:
Refs #1060 (left: the operator's device check below, and scope item 3, a Réglages line when iOS badges are off, which needs a wording decision)
Claim: mac/M1
Author model: Claude Opus 5.5 (mac/M1-i1060-opus)
Reviewer model: fable-5.2 (mac/M1-r1079-fable: APPROVE on bb5d7724 with comment fixes; APPROVE on 95dbe630, the head)

### Problem
No app icon badge with unread MPs (operator, 2026-11-17).

### Trace (dev-swift `1df2121a`)
- Launch: `RootNavigationView.swift:40` loads the forum list whatever the start tab, through `PrivateMessageCountingSource` (`RootModel.swift:159-166`, `PrivateMessageCount.swift:58-60`), which records the home page's count (`ForumListParser.swift:39`). `RootModel.appIconBadge` (`RootModel+Notifications.swift:7-10`) then has it and `RootNavigationView.swift:60-63` sets the icon. **Messages never needs to be opened**: the new hosted test of the real root shows it.
- Background: `MPBackgroundCheck.swift:60` sets the badge after each check (default interval 30 min, `SettingKey.swift:81`).
- Setting: `mp_badge_enabled` default true (`SettingKey.swift:78`); off gives 0.
- Permission: asked at launch (`SwiftHFRApp.swift:105`, `MPNotificationCenter.swift:17-30`).

### Cause found in the code (first launch only)
The root sets the badge only when its count changes. At a build's first launch, the home page's count can arrive while iOS's permission prompt is on screen. Measured on the iOS 27.0 simulator: with authorization `notDetermined`, `badgeSetting` is `notSupported` and `setBadgeCount` **does not throw**, so the write is dropped silently (the « Badge not set » log never fires). Nothing sets the badge again until the count changes. Legacy sets it again each time the app is back on screen (`MainWindow.swift:2588-2593` @ 87fe0d1c, `syncAppIconBadge` at `:1564-1567`).

This does not explain a build that never asked for permission (the operator's comment of 22:00: SwiftHFR missing from iOS Notifications): that remains cause 1, the build.

### Change
- `MPNotificationDelivering.setBadge` returns whether iOS shows the badge (`@discardableResult`): `MPNotificationCenter` reads `badgeSetting == .enabled` and the write's success.
- `RootNavigationView` takes the delivery as a parameter (default `MPNotificationCenter()`), keeps a badge iOS did not show pending, and sets it again when its window becomes active. A shown badge is not set again on every foreground (unlike legacy): the app's count can be older than the one the background check just set (GAP-192). Limit: a pending badge may rewrite such a newer count once, when a background check set it after badges were turned on while the badge was pending; the next page load corrects it. A refused permission keeps the badge pending: one settings read and one write per foreground.
- Why no wider: the count path is right (test below); Réglages is untouched (scope 3 needs a wording decision).

### Tests
- `AppIconBadgeHostedTests/theLaunchsHomePageGivesTheIconItsCountWithoutOpeningMessages()`: the real root hosted with a fake home page saying 3 unread; the icon gets 3, no MP list request. Passes before and after: it shows the launch path.
- `AppIconBadgeHostedTests/aBadgeIOSDidNotShowIsSetAgainWhenTheWindowIsBackOnScreen()`: iOS refuses the first write (no permission); after allowing and an `active` phase, the badge is set again; a later background/active round sets nothing more. **Fails without the fix** (run with the seam, before the fix: badges stayed `[3]`).
- `FakeMPDelivery` gained `badgeAllowed`; `MPNotificationOpenTests`, `PrivateMessageBadgeTests`, `MultiWindowTests` green.
- Whole `SwiftHFRTests`: 1916 tests in 246 suites passed (iOS 27.0 simulator).

### Device checks for the operator (build from this branch or dev-swift after merge; user2 or own account with unread MPs)
1. Delete the app, install, launch: the permission prompt appears. Allow with badges. Without opening Messages, the icon shows the unread count once the home page is loaded (go to the Home Screen to see it).
2. With the app in the background, after a background check (Réglages › Notifications MP shows « Dernière vérification »), the badge follows the count.
3. Read the MPs: the badge clears at 0.
4. iOS Réglages › Notifications › SwiftHFR › « Pastilles » off: the icon shows nothing; SwiftHFR's Réglages › Notifications MP says nothing about it today (scope 3, pending decision). Turn « Pastilles » back on and return to the app: the badge comes back.

### Ledger

```gap-edit
GAP-192
SwiftHFR final: Badge per setting, set by the running app and by the background check; a badge iOS did not show (no permission yet) is set again when the app is back on screen, a shown one is not (#1060).
Legacy ref: MPBackgroundService.swift:60-66; MainWindow.swift:1564-1567, :2588-2593
```

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (fable-5.2, mac/M1-r1079-fable, bb5d7724)** — APPROVE

The measurement is credible and the design does not depend on it: my probe in the test host (iOS 27.0 simulator, `authorizationStatus=0`, `badgeSetting=0` = `notSupported`) shows `setBadgeCount(3)` returns without throwing, so the `badgeSetting == .enabled` read is the only signal; a throw is also folded into `false`. `.notSupported` on an iPhone only appears under `notDetermined`; provisional is not requested; Focus modes do not touch `badgeSetting`. Legacy pointers checked at 87fe0d1c (`MainWindow.swift:1564-1567`, `:2588-2593`, `MPBackgroundService.swift:60-66`). Ledger block parses (`ledger.py check-body`) and its `SwiftHFR final` says exactly what the code does. Multi-window: `SharedPrivateMessageCounts` gives every root the same count per generation, so N windows only repeat the same write; a per-window `badgeIsPending` cannot set a count another window has moved past. Isolation: `View` is `@MainActor`, the `Task` writes `@State` there; compiles under strict concurrency. Lint by hand: no line over 140, no function over 50 lines, no nesting or discardable-let issue.

1. **Low** — `App/SwiftHFR/Root/RootNavigationView.swift:66-68`: the comment says "a newer count a background check set stays", which is not true for a *pending* badge. Scenario: iOS « Pastilles » off, count 3 pending; app in background, 2 more MPs arrive, the member turns « Pastilles » on, the background check writes 5; back to the app, the root rewrites its stale 3, and nothing reloads the count on foreground (`AppLifecycle.scenePhaseChanged` only rechecks sessions). Self-corrects at the next page load. Fix: state the limit in the comment (and PR body), or, when pending on `.active`, skip the write if the ledger's last recorded count is newer than the page that gave `appIconBadge` — the comment fix is enough for me.
2. **Detail** — same lines: a refused permission keeps `badgeIsPending` true for the life of the root, so every foreground costs one `notificationSettings()` + one `setBadgeCount`. Harmless, and it is what makes device check 4 work; the doc comment says "no permission yet" only — add "or refused".
3. **Detail** — `docs/lots/LOT-140-background-mp-check.md:70` ("the running app sets the icon badge from the Messages badge count") does not mention the re-set rule (#1060); one clause, same PR or the ledger note.
4. **Detail** — `theLaunchsHomePageGivesTheIconItsCountWithoutOpeningMessages` passes before and after, as the PR says: a characterization test of the count path, fine as such.

**Verified**: worktree at bb5d7724, `xcodebuild build test` on simulator 9AAF4FFD (`AppIconBadgeHostedTests`, `MPNotificationOpenTests`, `PrivateMessageBadgeTests`, `MultiWindowTests`, `MPBackgroundCheckTests`): 49 tests, 5 suites, green. Mutation: removed the `.active && badgeIsPending` re-set → `aBadgeIOSDidNotShowIsSetAgainWhenTheWindowIsBackOnScreen` fails (`again == [3, 3]` and `after == [3, 3]`, badges stay `[3]`); restored. Probe test (above) run in the same host. `python3 -I tooling/docs/ledger.py check-body --pr 1079`: 1 block ok. Worktree, DerivedData and logs removed.

**Adversarial review (fable-5.2, mac/M1-r1079-fable, delta 95dbe630)** — APPROVE

Delta over bb5d7724 is comments and one spec clause only: `App/SwiftHFR/Root/RootNavigationView.swift:21-23, 67-70` and `docs/lots/LOT-140-background-mp-check.md:70`. No code path changed, so no build.

- Comments match the code exactly: `MPNotificationCenter.setBadge` does one `notificationSettings()` read and one `setBadgeCount` per call, and a pending badge is written once per `.active`; "may rewrite such a count once" holds, since a shown rewrite clears `badgeIsPending` and a refused one means the background check's write was dropped too (no newer count to lose).
- LOT-140 clause states the re-set rule and its limit as the code has it; the legacy citation `MainWindow.swift:2588-2593 @ 87fe0d1c` is the `guard newValue == .active … Task { await syncAppIconBadge() }` block (checked at bb5d7724).
- PR body Change section says the same as the comments. Findings 1-3 of the bb5d7724 review closed; 4 was a note.
